purpose: Map predeclared validity evidence to STRONG/MODERATE/WEAK/INSUFFICIENT without over-filtering the candidate universe or converting every imperfect research dimension into a hard block.
primary_objective: Prefer strategies that improve matched-baseline post-cost expectancy and long-run growth while retaining usable candidate coverage and opportunity frequency.
hard_block_policy: Only system-critical integrity or discipline failures may force a hard block. Ordinary research weakness must not be promoted to a hard block.

coverage_guardrail.rule: A strategy may not be labeled stronger merely because tighter filters reduce candidate count. Any increase in apparent edge accompanied by materially lower coverage must be reported as an edge-coverage tradeoff rather than an unconditional improvement.
coverage_guardrail.low_coverage_semantics: Low coverage is normally a downgrade or uncertainty flag, not a hard block, unless it makes the experiment statistically uninterpretable under the preregistered sample design.

INSUFFICIENT: Required evidence is missing, sample information is too sparse for the preregistered claim, or integrity of the validity assessment cannot be established.
A strategy with near-zero usable coverage and too few observations to estimate edge may be INSUFFICIENT even if observed hit rate is high.
WEAK: Some positive baseline-relative evidence exists but is small, unstable, concentrated, cost-sensitive, parameter-sensitive, or coverage-constrained.
WEAK evidence may still produce candidates; it is not equivalent to a system failure.
MODERATE: Positive post-cost advantage versus matched baseline is visible across more than one important validity dimension and survives reasonable perturbations, with usable coverage.
Some weaknesses may remain if they are explicit and do not dominate the claim.
STRONG: Positive post-cost baseline-relative advantage is replicated out of sample, broadly stable across relevant regimes and securities, robust to reasonable parameter variation and execution costs, and achieved without collapsing candidate coverage.
STRONG does not mean guaranteed profitability.

anti_and_gate_rule: STRONG/MODERATE/WEAK are not computed by requiring every soft validity dimension to pass a fixed threshold. Dimensions contribute evidence and uncertainty; only hard blockers are binary.

threshold_policy.reason: Absolute thresholds such as win-rate > 55%, Sharpe > 1, or selection-rate > X% would be arbitrary across strategies and could create permanent no-trade behavior.
threshold_policy.experiment_specific_thresholds: Any numeric thresholds needed for a concrete experiment must be preregistered before outcome inspection and justified relative to its matched baseline, sample size, horizon, turnover and execution design.

baseline_policy.random_baseline: Random selection must be matched on universe, dates, holding horizon, execution assumptions and transaction costs. A 50% ten-day hit-rate baseline is a null intuition, not a permanently hardcoded empirical fact.

decision_binding.STRONG: Eligible for Discipline Engine consideration subject to risk rules.
decision_binding.MODERATE: Eligible for Discipline Engine consideration subject to risk rules and any preregistered position-size limitations.
decision_binding.WEAK: Risk-increasing actions are not automatically authorized; experiment-specific decision policy applies. Risk-reducing actions remain permitted subject to Discipline Engine.
decision_binding.INSUFFICIENT: Risk-increasing actions map to NO_ACTION_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. Risk-reducing actions remain permitted subject to Discipline Engine.

non_goals: No maximizing hit rate by eliminating almost all trades
No replacing matched-baseline expectancy with a single headline metric
